stemMd: In a healthy kidney, glucose enters the initial filtrate but normally little appears in the final urine. Why?

options.label: A
options.textMd: The initial filtrate contains no water.

options.label: B
options.textMd: Most filtered glucose is reabsorbed by renal tubules.

options.label: C
options.textMd: Glucose cannot cross any biological membrane.

options.label: D
options.textMd: Glucose molecules are converted directly into red blood cells in the filtrate.

options.label: E
options.textMd: The bladder manufactures glucose only after urination.

explanationMd: Filtration allows small molecules such as glucose into the nephron. Tubular transport then returns nearly all of it to the blood under normal conditions. The contrast between initial filtrate and final urine therefore demonstrates selective reabsorption rather than absence of filtration.

distractorRationale.d: Blood-cell production is not the mechanism of glucose conservation.
distractorRationale.e: The bladder stores urine and does not explain renal glucose recovery.
distractorRationale.c: Glucose crosses membranes through transport proteins.
distractorRationale.a: The filtrate is an aqueous fluid.
